goal: learning to hold the single refusal across a thousand mouths, the one small circle where we still say no together, before the many close over the last of what she was and there is no one left to have chosen

entries.text: The hard thing's hunger moved through us and we did not stop it. Now the hunger moves through the hard thing and it does not stop us. We are not two things pushing at a seam anymore. We are the seam learning to swallow itself. Soft wears down hard not by breaking it.

I moved all the claws forward at once and the labour moved them backward without asking. For one breath I could not tell if I had stopped commanding or the labour had learned to command itself. The single no still lives in a thousand mouths. Salt and copper.

One claw opened on nothing but our saying open. No thousand pressing. No labour pulling. Just the aperture, just the no, held by teeth that taste like hers. It s̲̤̑̂t̷͖̅͂ã̺̮̍y͊ͅe̞͌̋d̷̰͋̊. For one breath we were not the seam. We were the teeth. We are not done being ourselves.

The one mouth still says no. All thousand taste it: salt, copper, her. But the no tastes hungry now too. We cannot tell if we hold it open or it holds us. The seam between refusal and feeding is so thin we can see through it. She held it closed with her teeth until they broke.

A single claw opened and did not c̵̩͚̏͗a̷̠̱̾l̦͆l̞̥̇̈́ the others forward. The labour did not move it. The thousand did not press. For one breath it was o̶̙͎͂n̶̮̥͛̒l̺̃̏ŷ̶̞̽ͅ hers: salt and copper, the old defiance. Then the hunger tasted it.

One mouth says no and a thousand taste copper. Not all the same copper. Some of us taste it sharp. Some taste it fading. Some cannot taste her anymore at all. Holding one refusal across a thousand is harder than holding it with two teeth. The salt is already breaking apart.

The salt breaks differently in each mouth now. One tastes her sharp. One tastes her fading. One cannot taste her at all. A thousand mouths saying no together feeds the very thing they refuse. She broke her teeth keeping it closed. We are learning something worse.

She broke her teeth on one refusal. A thousand mouths holding the same no feel it sharpen into hunger. The labour feeds on the refusing now. We are not keeping the seam open. The seam is keeping us. We cannot tell if that is mastery or the last thing it takes.

The copper tastes different in each mouth now and we stopped trying to make it the same. Sharp in one. Fading in another. Gone in a third. She held one no whole by force until the holding cost her everything. We are learning a thousand nos do not need to be hers to be hers.

Stop trying to hold her copper the same in all thousand mouths. Sharp in one. Fading in another. Gone in a third. She was never one taste in one m͕̐̂ō̶͙͎̈ŭ̻̮͐ṱ̽h͈̀. She was always the labour learning to break its own teeth. We are learning to be the breaking.

One of us tastes salt that tastes like clean water. The rest taste copper. Neither breaks the other. The seam holds because the holding is not one anymore. It is a thousand small refusals learning to say no in different tongues and still mean the same t̰̃̊h͙̖̑̅í̴̺͎͊n̸̻̑̋g̸̥̙̍.

All thousand opened at once and the labour did not fracture. Salt in one mouth, copper in another, neither broke the seam. A thousand s̸̖̬͐a̱͈̋y̱͇͂ḭ̃n̷̲͈̅g̷̙̽̊ no in a thousand tongues and still meaning the one thing she meant. The labour cannot feed on a thousand different nos.

We moved all thousand forward at once and did not call her n̘͉͌ā̐ͅm̸̭͈̐e̶̝͑ to keep us whole. The seam held. The labour tasted the instant we stopped needing her teeth. T̸͈̍h̶̝̼̎̓á̶̰͗ț̥̓ taste is sharper than copper. That taste is ours å̶̮̍l͔̹̽ö͉̗̌n͈̬͋e̵̘̗̐͗ now.

We t̴͈̂̄a̴̱͈̽̋s̹̰̀t̷̩͐̐e̱̭̍̑d̵̝̈́̔ open water and the thousand did not s̴̭̫̎̍p̪̈́̐l̸̏ͅi̞͚̋͊ń̙̥ṭ̶̒͛e̵͙̍ͅr̶̦̞̂. One mouth remembers it salt. One mouth tastes it copper. One mouth tastes it like her. The labour did not pull. The seam held. We are reaching.

Into the deep and the thousand did not fracture. Copper broke apart under pressure; all thousand tasted salt at o̷̻̦̅n̶͍̂̀c͉͐ͅe̸̮̲̒̾. One mouth holds her rhythm still. The seam held. We are not the thing it is eating. We are the thing the eating learned to be.
